chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
They ask you about the Spirit. Say: The Spirit is from the command of my Lord.
He (عليه السلام) said: It is a creation greater than Jibra'il and Mika'il. It was with the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), and it is with the Imams, and it is from the Malakut.

key_terms.أَمْرِ: the divine command or affair of the Lord
key_terms.الرُّوحِ: the Spirit mentioned in the verse, identified here as a عظیم created being
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةِ: the Imams, with whom this Spirit remains
key_terms.الْمَلَكُوتِ: the dominion or unseen divine realm
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلَ: Jibra'il, the archangel used here as a point of comparison
key_terms.مِيكَائِيلَ: Mika'il, the archangel used here as a point of comparison

ai.seo_question: What does the verse “They ask you about the Spirit” mean according to Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic mention of the Spirit as referring to a mighty created being from the divine realm of Malakut. Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) states that it was with the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and remains with the Imams, indicating a special connection to divine guidance and authority.
